The second beta of CoSky 8.0. It fixes a Redis Sentinel failover that beta.1 did not follow. The API stays frozen as [beta.1](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/releases/tag/v8.0.0-beta.1) set out. It is still a preview, for trying rather than real traffic. The stable release is still 6.x, on the [`v6`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/tree/v6) branch.

## Fixed

- **A Redis Sentinel failover is followed when the master hangs.**
  - beta.1 asked the Sentinels for the master only when it connected. A master that hung kept its connections open, so the namespaces stayed unavailable until it answered again, each request failing after a minute. In a local test that was not within 240 seconds.
  - The server now follows what the Sentinels announce. It took about 16 seconds, as on a Cluster.
- **A command the Redis driver cancels is `STORE_UNAVAILABLE`.** When the driver moves to another node, it cancels the commands still waiting on the old connection. Those came out as an internal error (500). Worse, they could end a loop following a namespace, as if it had been asked to stop.

## Changed

- **A command waits at most 5 seconds for Redis by default, on a single node and on Sentinel too,** as on a Cluster since beta.1, unless the URI sets its own `timeout`. A request on a Redis that hangs fails with `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` after 5 seconds rather than a minute.
- **On Sentinel, the server keeps a connection to each Sentinel**, to hear of a failover. The Sentinels must stay reachable, not only at start.

[Deployment](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment) now shows how to give the server Redis credentials and TLS, and a restricted ACL user that is enough, tried on a single node, Sentinel and a Cluster.

## Upgrading from beta.1

- Nothing to do: the wire format, the data in Redis and the properties are unchanged.
- A URI that counted on the driver's default of 60 seconds can say `?timeout=60s`.

## For those using the server's modules

`RedisStore.sentinel(client, uri)` is new, and `RedisStore.open` uses it for a Sentinel URI.

## Known limits

- **Tried on one laptop, not in a data center:** the Cluster and Sentinel failovers, the scale and the emulated network on the [Performance](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/performance) page. OIDC was tried with Keycloak 26 only.
- **On Sentinel, while a master that hangs still holds the connection hints come on,** each replica reads every namespace every second instead, so a write takes up to a second to reach watchers.
- **At rest, each replica reads each namespace once a second,** in case a hint was lost. On one Redis, 5,000 namespaces and three replicas took 30% of its CPU. A Cluster, or a longer `cosky.store.redis.tail-poll-interval`, lowers it.
- **Writes over a lossy network:** where 1% of packets are lost, a write's p99 is above 200 ms, as TCP waits to resend a lost packet.
- **A replica cut off from Redis on its own** goes on serving what it last knew, and stays ready. [Deployment](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment) shows how to notice.
